senses.definition: In an obvious or clearly apparent manner.
examples: She was in floods of tears and obviously very upset.
She'd obviously not gone to sleep yet: her eyes were bloodshot with sleepiness.
The plane has obviously been delayed.

quotes.text: It was a casual sneer, obviously one of a long line. There was hatred behind it, but of a quiet, chronic type, nothing new or unduly virulent, and he was taken aback by the flicker of amazed incredulity that passed over the younger man's ravaged face.
quotes.reference: 1963, Margery Allingham, chapter 8, in The China Governess: A Mystery, London: Chatto & Windus, →OCLC:

quotes.text: She came in now, but to the closet; from it she took a simple skirt and blouse. Picking up her underclothing she departed, obviously to dress somewhere else.

senses.definition: (colloquial) Used as a filler word, or to introduce information even when not obvious.
examples: You weren't to know, but I've spoken to, obviously, Jim about this, and ...
